title: Find the Longest Balanced Substring of a Binary String
summary: Given a binary string, find the longest substring where the number of zeroes equals the number of ones, and all zeroes precede all ones.
statement: Given a binary string, find the longest substring where the number of zeroes equals the number of ones, and all zeroes precede all ones. The empty substring is considered balanced. Return the length of this longest balanced substring.
constraints: A balanced substring consists of some zeros followed by the same number of ones.
The zero and one blocks must each be contiguous and nonempty.
Return the maximum balanced substring length, or zero if none exists.
hints: Only the boundary between a zero run and its following one run matters.
Count zeros in the current zero run and ones in the following one run.
At each one, a balanced suffix uses twice the smaller run count; reset both counts when zeros resume after ones.
Every valid substring lies at one such run boundary, and taking the smaller count is both feasible and maximal there.
editorial: Every valid substring lies at one such run boundary, and taking the smaller count is both feasible and maximal there.

tests.explanation: The final 000111 block is balanced and has length six.
Two zeros followed by the first two ones form a length-four balanced substring.
